# bibelot

Floating desktop widgets, written in **Rust**, **GTK4** and **GNU Guile Scheme**.

A *bibelot* is a small decorative object: the thing on a desk that is there to
be looked at and picked up, not to hold the desk together.  These are the cards
that float over a Wayland desktop -- a clock, the weather, a note -- and the
machinery that keeps them placed, refreshed and skinned.

This is the widget engine split out of [[https://github.com/jjbigorra/whelk][whelk]].  Whelk remains the host: it
owns the settings language, the application and the first bar's palette.  The
cards, their readings, their placement file and their own Scheme theme live
here.

## What it does

- Sixteen card kinds: Clock, Calendar, Weather, Batteries, Notes, Reminders,
  World Clock, Stocks, Now Playing, Visualizer, Media, Photos, Files, News,
  System and Custom.
- One bottom-layer surface per card, anchored at its configured or saved
  position, moved by its grip, snapped to an 8 px grid and clamped into its
  monitor.
- A per-monitor state file (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/bibelot/widgets-<stem>.ini`) so a
  drag survives a restart; an unplugged monitor falls back to the last place
  the card was seen.
- The readings themselves: sysfs batteries, `/proc` CPU and memory, MPRIS
  players, cava frames, Open-Meteo weather, Yahoo quotes, RSS/Atom news, photo
  folders, the recent-documents XBEL and the reminders model.
- A Scheme theme for the card's structural values and a final stylesheet.

## Build and test

GTK4, `gtk4-layer-shell`, GNU Guile 3.0 development files and `pkg-config` are
needed.

```sh
cargo build
cargo test
cargo fmt --check
```

The GTK cards themselves need a Wayland session; the suite covers the data,
geometry, state, theme and the Scheme module without one.  A card can be tried
inside whelk, which is its intended host.

## Install

```sh
scripts/install.sh --prefix=/usr/local
```

The installer stages `(bibelot theme)` and the documentation; the Rust library
is built by its host.  `default.nix`, `guix.scm` and `manifest.scm` provide the
standalone Nix package, Guix package and development shell.  WheLK carries a
pinned source snapshot of this crate under `rust/vendor/bibelot`, so the host
can build offline without a sibling checkout.

## The host contract

`bibelot::Widgets::build` takes the GTK application, the typed card configs, a
`bibelot::Skin`, a `bibelot::Theme` and the settings file path.  The host maps
its own bar palette and frosted-glass settings into the skin; a card that names
its own `#:foreground`, `#:background`, `#:accent`, `#:opacity`, `#:blur`,
`#:radius`, `#:shine`, `#:reflection` or `#:flare` changes only what it named.
The card classes keep the `whelk-widget-*` names so settings written for the
shell before the split still select them.

## The Scheme theme

`scheme/bibelot/theme.scm` carries the defaults.  It returns an alist from
`widget-theme`:

```scheme
(configure-widgets! #:card-padding 18
                    #:card-gap 12
                    #:extra-css ".whelk-widget-clock-time { font-size: 34px; }")
```

`card-padding` and `card-gap` are pixels, and `extra-css` is appended after the
structural stylesheet.  A user file passed to `Guile::theme` is evaluated inside
the module, so it needs no import; a file that raises is reported and the
defaults are used instead of half a theme.

A host that already runs Guile (whelk does) should ask its own runtime for
`(bibelot theme)` and build a `Theme` with `Theme::from_alist`; initializing a
second Guile runtime in the same process is not possible.  `Guile::init` is for
a host with no Guile of its own.

The user file is `BIBELOT_THEME`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bibelot/theme.scm`
(`~/.config/bibelot/theme.scm`).  `theme::user_theme_path()` is the one
resolver for hosts that want to read it themselves.

`BIBELOT_SCHEME_DIR` points the loader at a development or staged module tree.
Debug builds also find the checkout; a release install looks in
`<prefix>/share/guile/site/3.0` and `/usr/share/guile/site/3.0`.

## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
| --- | --- |
| `src/widgets.rs` | the kind catalogue, geometry, pure readings and the typed config |
| `src/desktopwidgets.rs` | the GTK surfaces, drag, timers and the manager |
| `src/widgetstate.rs` | the placement and per-widget state file |
| `src/batterybar.rs`, `src/cpubar.rs`, `src/memorybar.rs` | the system readings |
| `src/mpris.rs`, `src/command.rs`, `src/format.rs`, `src/json.rs`, `src/sources.rs` | the readers the cards share |
| `src/visualizer.rs` | one cava process per visualizer card |
| `src/skin.rs`, `src/style.rs`, `src/frost.rs` | the host palette turned into a card stylesheet |
| `src/theme.rs`, `src/guile.rs` | `(bibelot theme)` and the standalone Guile boundary |
| `scheme/bibelot/theme.scm` | the Scheme defaults and `configure-widgets!` |
| `docs/widgets.org` | the engine's internals and host contract |
